title: SACHI: A Stationarity-Aware, All-Digital, Near-Memory, Ising Architecture
problem: Prior Ising accelerators for solving NP-complete problems require complex analog/digital converters (ADCs/DACs), suffer from reliability issues due to process-variation-sensitive embedded memory, and are limited to specific problem classes. These designs lack tight integration with general-purpose CPUs.
motivation: Ising machines have demonstrated capability for solving complex real-world optimization problems, but current dedicated accelerators are unreliable and have limited practical applicability without eliminating their architectural bottlenecks.
method: SACHI repurposes CPU L1 cache as an Ising compute engine using all-digital SRAM-based in-memory processing, eliminating ADCs/DACs and enabling tight CPU pipeline integration. It implements reuse-aware compute strategies and novel mapping strategies optimized for high-precision optimization workloads.
key_novelty: All-digital Ising architecture that repurposes existing CPU L1 cache hardware to provide acceleration with minimal overhead while eliminating the reliability and complexity issues of prior designs.
contributions: All-digital Ising accelerator using repurposed L1 cache and in-memory SRAM processing
Eliminates analog/digital converters and improves reliability over BRIM baseline
Achieves higher parallelism through reuse-aware compute design
Novel compute and mapping strategies for large-scale high-precision optimization problems
limitations: Limitations of the all-digital approach and applicability beyond the four demonstrated optimization problems (asset allocation, molecular dynamics, image segmentation, TSP) not discussed.
